subject: Zuora renewal + NetSuite sync: termination language & migration risk
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Zuora renewal + NetSuite sync: termination language & migration risk

Quick summary: Zuora renewal is coming up in July. Their rep (Emily) just sent over a draft SOW and three renewal options. Main risk: our NetSuite connector has custom mapping that Zuora flags as "unsupported" under their standard onboarding. If we need to rip-and-replace to a supported flow, migration could be 6-8 weeks and ~ $75k professional services.

What I need from this group:
- Laura: legal/contract ask — can we get a carve-out for the existing NetSuite mapping so we avoid a forced migration clause?
- Marissa: finance — can you surface the budget for migration (capex vs. services)?
- Ben: ops — if we decide to move off Zuora, how long to implement Stripe/Chargebee proof-of-concept for invoice + NS sync?

I've attached the SOW they sent and a quick estimate from our infra team. Emily is on cc and will follow up with renewal pricing.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Zuora_SOW_2027.pdf (application/pdf), NS_sync_migration_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@zuora.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procure@financeops-llc.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zuora renewal + NetSuite sync: termination language & migration risk

Hi Karthik — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the internal estimate. Quick responses below:

- The draft SOW we shared is the standard onboarding package. We can offer a 90-day grace period for customers who need to maintain their existing NS customization while we scope a migration, but it requires an explicit addendum (we've attached a one-page addendum template).
- Professional services estimate you saw from our side (we use a partner) is usually lower than $75k, but that assumes the mapping is inside the supported connector framework. If you have bespoke transforms, the partner will bill for custom scripts.
- Renewal pricing options: 1) 12-month renewal with 3% increase; 2) 24-month with 7% discount; 3) 36-month enterprise with included PS hours (we can trade for a 12-month free trial of our advanced reporting).

I'll drop the addendum and a compact SOW (pdf + txt) to make edits easier. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your technical lead to walk the connector constraints.

Best,
Emily Zhang
Senior Account Executive, Zuora

Attachments: Zuora_renewal_options.txt

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zuora renewal + NetSuite sync: termination language & migration risk

Karthik — looping legal. High level thoughts:

1) Do not accept a clause that allows unilateral enforcement of connector changes that mandate migration within the renewal period. We can accept a remediation timeline but it must be tied to mutually agreed acceptance tests.
2) Ask for an explicit rollback clause if Zuora's connector update causes invoice/regression for 10%+ of a sampled billing cohort.
3) We should request the 90-day grace period as a minimum and add a cap on PS day rates for bespoke work in the addendum.

Marissa — from finance perspective, if we have to pay up to $75k, is that moveable into this fiscal quarter? If not, can we use reserved funds or request an exception?

I'll draft a short redline for the addendum and share by EOD.

Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zuora renewal + NetSuite sync: termination language & migration risk

Thanks — quick budget note: current FY27 vendor contingency includes a $100k bucket for unforeseen billing platform work. We can cover the $75k migration cost in Q2 without impacting hiring plans, but we'll need exec sign-off for any contract language that increases our recurring commitment.

Two asks for the team:
- Karthik/Laura: prioritize getting the addendum and capped PS day-rate into the SOW before we sign.
- Ben: please confirm the Ops estimate (I saw the spreadsheet) and a fallback timeline for a different billing provider. If Ops indicates >12 weeks for a migration to an alternate platform, we'll add time in our risk calc.

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: NS_sync_migration_estimate.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zuora renewal + NetSuite sync: termination language & migration risk

On Thu, 6 May 2027 10:30:00 -07:00, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Quick summary: Zuora renewal is coming up in July. Their rep (Emily) just sent over a draft SOW and three renewal options. Main risk: our NetSuite connector has custom mapping that Zuora flags as "unsupported" under their standard onboarding. If we need to rip-and-replace to a supported flow, migration could be 6-8 weeks and ~ $75k professional services.

Ben here — dug in with infra and billing team. Realistic notes: if we accept Zuora's addendum and cap the PS day-rate, we can probably keep current mapping live for the renewal window with minimal changes (1-2 weeks of effort) and then run a parallel migration plan that takes ~10 weeks to finish (build -> test -> cutover).

Alternate platform to de-risk: spinning up Chargebee + middleware to NetSuite would be a 12-16 week project and similar cost profile. Stripe billing isn't a viable source-of-truth for our multi-entity NetSuite flows without significant custom work.

Suggested immediate steps:
- Laura: send redline to Emily with the 90-day grace + capped PS day-rate + rollback test.
- Marissa: confirm budget sign-off (looks good from me).
- Karthik: schedule a 30-min call with Emily + our billing lead next week to lock the addendum language.

I'll stand up a migration plan doc and share a timeline by Monday.

Ben Carter
Head of Billing Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@zuora.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 May 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zuora renewal + NetSuite sync: termination language & migration risk

Thanks team — appreciate the fast responses. Per our call notes this morning (attached), Zuora will:

- Provide the 90-day grace addendum with a capped day-rate for partner PS (we'll include a $200/hr cap by default; can be reduced in negotiation).
- Add explicit rollback acceptance criteria tied to invoice parity testing (sample cohort).
- Offer a 30% discount on PS if you commit to a 24-month renewal at the enterprise tier.

Next steps: I'll upload the addendum redline to DocuSign and send a short SOW revision. Karthik — if you can confirm by EOD Wednesday that legal's redline is acceptable, we can lock the renewal pricing and avoid any forced migration clause in the contract term.

Best,
Emily
Senior Account Executive, Zuora

Attachments: Renewal_call_notes_09052027.txt, Zuora_addendum_draft.pdf
